name: Heca
goal:
Consolidare Heca come workspace compositor nativo, keyboard-first e pluggable, completando piattaforma terminale, architettura chrome/plugin, libreria grid-ui, integrazione Neovim GUI e rifiniture app/chrome.
The gates before any code
- §0 pre-flight, three written answers, per thing touched: which existing widget does this → if none, which planner task covers it (quote the id) → if neither, it is a proposal, not a commit.
- §0b widget vs component: if it can be built inside heca-grid-ui, it belongs there. A component only leaves the library because it binds an app concept.
- §0c the event system is DOM-shaped — capture → target → bubble, keys do bubble, a widget never hit-tests and never forwards, nothing focused means nothing delivered, and a cursor inside a container is not focus. Reach for a handler before an intent, a policy arm or a registry.
- ⭐⭐ Rule Zero: write the line a plugin author would type. A registry, an id or a crate-private type means the API is missing. HintTargetRegistry, HintTargets, HintTargetId, Base::hint_target, named_press are gone and must not come back.
description: Compositore di workspace GPU-native per sviluppatori, ispirato al layout a colonne scrollabili di Niri, che unifica terminali, editor e strumenti in una singola finestra accelerata via GPU. Think tmux meets Niri meets Neovide: terminali, editor e futuri container/plugin convivono nello stesso frame con animazioni fluide, testo nitido e chrome renderizzato via GPU.

projectGuidelines.content:
## Migrated legacy project rules

### Global rules
- Per UI nuove usare widget esistenti di heca-grid-ui o introdurre widget generici theme-driven in heca-grid-ui, non composizioni ad-hoc nell'app.
- Ogni azione utente deve passare per ActionRegistry e KeymapRegistry, con keybinding configurabili.
- Nessun hardcode di colori, keybinding o stile: leggere da Theme/config.
- Ogni capability significativa deve essere raggiungibile da mouse/UI, keyboard/action e RPC quando appropriato.
- PRE-FLIGHT before any UI code, answered in writing: (1) which existing widget/function/action does this — name it; (2) if none, which planner task covers it — search the PIECES, not just the feature, and quote the id; (3) if neither, it is a proposal, not a commit — and it gets filed in the planner, never left in a prose list.
- WIDGET vs COMPONENT — capability decides, not size. If it can be built inside heca-grid-ui it is a widget and lives there (a UI library also ships Dialog, Select, ContextMenu, CommandPalette). A COMPONENT composes widgets AND binds an app concept (Intent, action name, drag id, hint target id, chrome signal, nav_key) and lives in heca/src/components/. A composition that binds none of those is a widget in the wrong crate.
- Composition inside heca-grid-ui is REAL CHILDREN in Base.children — the framework walks them (layout, paint, capture/bubble). ViewNode describes a tree as DATA for plugins/config/RPC and is realized ABOVE the library; it is unavailable inside grid-ui (heca-view-realize depends on heca-grid-ui). Hand-painting a composition is never the answer.
- A component takes plain data plus the seams it binds (Intent/emitter, &mut BuildCx, an action NAME, the theme) and NEVER &AppState — AppState needs a window, so a component taking it cannot be tested. Every component ships one headless unit test asserting the built tree or the painted scene, never a flag.
- Never re-compose an existing shape inline in chrome/, a provider, the sidebar or a plugin. Import the component; if you need a variation, add a builder to it. Copying a composition is how a row shape becomes unreachable outside the file that drew it.
- WORKING WITH ANTONIO — REUSE WIDGETS. This is the recurring frustration and it has been earned repeatedly. Do not solve a text problem inside a widget that draws text: the palette hand-rolled truncation, then wrapping, then match highlighting, then a matcher, each because the shared piece did not exist. Search for the shared piece first; if it is missing, build it in heca-grid-ui.
- WORKING WITH ANTONIO — Nothing hardcoded that is data. The recurring defect: solved for the one case in front of the author, wrong the moment the model is used as designed (a focus key naming a SIDE, a scroll offset keyed by container KIND, a shell owning a scroll area that belongs to whoever nests one).
- WORKING WITH ANTONIO — Answer questions before writing code. If Antonio asks 'what do you mean' or 'is it doable', reply first. 'We are discussing' means STOP WRITING — including reverts, because a revert is a write.
- WORKING WITH ANTONIO — Antonio verifies anything visual themselves, and will spot what tests cannot (the ToggleLe ftSidebar mark rendering bug came from a screenshot, not the suite). Green tests never verify layout, overlay, scroll or interaction. Assert what was reported: if a bug was visible, measure the visible thing — a test asserting a grow FLAG passed while the layout was visibly broken.
- WORKING WITH ANTONIO — Never decide whether a task lives or dies: ask. Do not act on an instruction's letter when the next step needs otherwise.
- WORKING WITH ANTONIO — Do not defer. 'Its own phase' or 'a follow-up' is not an answer unless Antonio chooses it, and size is not a reason to defer. 'Do it now' means now.
- WORKING WITH ANTONIO — Commit messages say what changed. Prior-error archaeology belongs in the planner task, not the commit message or the PR body.
- GIT — After a PR merges, branch from the UPDATED main. Committing onto an already-merged branch strands the work, and rewriting a merged PR's description falsifies the record of something already shipped. Never do either.
- GIT — `git checkout <file>` has destroyed uncommitted work twice. Copy to the scratchpad first. A global find-and-replace also broke code outside its intent: bound every edit.
- FACT (SDK) — The drift guard demands a builder for every #[prop] (heca-view-realize's every_widget_property_is_reachable_from_the_sdk); fix by adding one in heca-view/src/build.rs. A host_only prop (a list, a composed value) is exempt. u8 is NOT an accepted prop type; u16/usize/f32 are.
- FACT (layout) — LayoutEngine resolves the inherited font DURING layout, so a label inside a Flex resolves to font 13.5, not 15 (size-variant scaling). Read base().font AFTER layout; measuring with the pre-layout font is off by a character.
- FACT (layout) — Taffy rounds every box to whole pixels: a label measured at 105.3px is handed 105.0, and a label that cannot fit its own text cuts it. mono_cells carries a half-pixel slack for this. Separately, a box sized to an exact number of cells divides to n − ε in f64 and floors one short — the fit needs an epsilon.
- FACT (layout) — flex_grow alone does NOT divide a region: it distributes only positive free space, so two containers measured 1214px each inside a 600px body. A share needs a zero base size PLUS permission to shrink (CSS flex: 1 1 0). Layout has no flex_basis yet.
- FACT (layout) — A size that only CAPS a viewport fraction is not a size: 'normal' and 'large' were identical below ~1550px because 0.55 × viewport sat under both caps, and the test passed at 1800px where they happened to differ. Assert at an ordinary window size.
- FACT (text) — The shaper drops a text run's leading whitespace, so splitting a line into runs at mark boundaries walks every space in the label; marks are over-drawn per character for this reason. Scene-level tests cannot see it — the runs they assert are correct and the loss is in shaping.
- FACT (overlays) — Overlay layers are laid out every frame (heca/src/chrome/mod.rs layout_layers runs LayoutEngine::compute on each visible layer root), so layer children get real measured bounds. Select is the precedent for an overlay with real children (select.rs:188, :365, :554): measured in the widget's own flow, then shifted to absolute targets in the panel.
- FACT (persistence) — Clearing a persisted store cannot just empty it in memory: the next save merges the disk back in. Rewrite the file instead (search_state::forget). forget_on_disk is split from forget only because forget takes &mut AppState, which cannot exist in a test.
- FACT (planner) — Handoffs live on phase.handoff; .planner/HANDOFF.md is deprecated. resume.json's nextSteps/notes are stale free text that task operations never refresh and have misdirected multiple sessions: READ THE TASK. planner-task-show / planner-phase-update can exceed the tool output limit (the response is saved to a file, and phase-update APPLIES even when it cannot be displayed). Phase status is derived from tasks, so a phase JSON keeps status: null while the tool reports done. planner-task-complete fails on an unticked checklist; force: true is the way when the work shipped without it. ALWAYS check task status against the commits — finished tasks have sat in-progress for a whole session.
